housing.summary: Singapore's rental market is expensive and fast-moving. Expats typically rent private condominiums or HDB flats; a central-district (Core Central Region: Orchard, River Valley, Tanjong Pagar) one-bedroom condo commands premium rents. Standard leases run 12-24 months. The market is dominated by agents and portals like PropertyGuru and 99.co.

banking.summary: Opening a bank account is straightforward for residents holding an Employment Pass or S Pass. Major banks are DBS/POSB, OCBC, and UOB, alongside international banks like Standard Chartered, HSBC, and Citibank. Foreigners generally need passport, work pass, proof of address, and sometimes a minimum initial deposit.
required_docs: Employment Pass / S Pass or valid work permit

schools.summary: Singapore has a large international school sector serving expat families, offering IB, British, American, and other national curricula. Well-known international schools include UWCSEA, Tanglin Trust School, Singapore American School, and Dulwich College. Local public schools follow the Singapore national curriculum but have limited places for foreigners. Demand is high and waiting lists are common.

legal_admin.summary: Foreign workers must hold a valid work pass (Employment Pass, S Pass, or Work Permit) issued by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) before working. After arrival, pass holders complete registration and receive their pass card; those staying long-term may register for identification. The employer typically sponsors and initiates the pass application.
legal_admin.registration_step: Obtain and register a valid work pass (Employment Pass / S Pass / Work Permit) via the Ministry of Manpower

tax_finance.summary: Income tax is administered by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). Singapore has a progressive resident income tax system with relatively low rates and no capital gains tax. Tax residency generally depends on days present in the country. Individuals are identified for tax by their NRIC (locals/PRs) or FIN (foreigners on passes).
tax_finance.tax_id_name: Tax Reference Number (NRIC for residents / FIN for foreigners)

transport.summary: Singapore has an extensive, efficient public transport network of MRT (metro) and buses, operated under a unified fare system. Travelers pay via contactless bank cards or the EZ-Link/SimplyGo stored-value card. Car ownership is very expensive due to the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) system. Foreigners can drive on a valid foreign or international licence short-term, then must convert to a Singapore licence.
transport.network_name: MRT and public bus network (SMRT / SBS Transit)
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Foreign licence holders must convert to a Singapore driving licence (often via the Basic Theory Test) through the Traffic Police / LTA within the permitted period
transport.healthcare_registration: No universal registration for foreigners; employers must provide medical insurance for pass holders. Residents/PRs contribute to MediSave/CPF. Care is delivered via public polyclinics/hospitals and private providers, largely pay-as-you-go with insurance.
